content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published guidelines for the treatment of syphilis, caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for drug therapy and management of this sexually transmitted infection (STI). The publication is cataloged under the WHO Library with the ISBN 978-92-4-154980-6 and classified under NLM classification WC 170. The document was released in 2016, and all rights are reserved by the WHO. The designations and presentation of material in this publication do not imply any opinion by the WHO regarding the legal status of any country, territory, city, or area, or its authorities, nor do they address the delimitation of its frontiers or boundaries. Any dotted or dashed lines on maps represent approximate borderlines, which may not yet have full agreement. The mention of specific companies or manufacturers’ products does not imply endorsement or recommendation by the WHO over others of a similar nature that are not mentioned. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters. While the WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information in this publication, the material is distributed without warranty of any kind, either expressed or implied. The responsibility for the interpretation and use of the material lies with the reader, and the WHO shall not be held liable for damages arising from its use. The guidelines were developed with input from a diverse group of experts from various regions and institutions. These experts declared their potential conflicts of interest, including involvement in related academic work, commercial financial interests, indirect commercial financial interests, and non-commercial interests or grants. The declarations were reviewed to ensure transparency and minimize bias in the guideline development process. For example: Dr. Yaw Adu-Sarkodie from Ghana declared no conflicts of interest. Dr. Andrew Amato from Sweden also declared no conflicts of interest. Dr. John Changalucha from Tanzania disclosed prior research support from GSK for evaluating HPV vaccine safety and immunogenicity, which ended in 2011 and was unrelated to the STI guidelines. Dr. Craig Cohen from the USA disclosed consulting work for the development of new drugs for bacterial vaginosis with Symbiomix Inc. Dr. Suzanne Garland from Australia disclosed financial awards and research grants related to HPV vaccine trials and surveillance, but these were unrelated to syphilis treatment. Dr. Jeffrey Klausner from the USA disclosed receiving syphilis test kits and travel support from diagnostic companies, but no commercial recommendations were made in the guidelines. The WHO guidelines aim to provide clear, evidence-based recommendations for the treatment of syphilis while ensuring transparency and minimizing conflicts of interest among contributors.
